Patched crates.io snapshots used through `[patch.crates-io]` in the workspace
or experiment `Cargo.toml`. Each directory is the pristine crate plus one patch file in
[`patches/`](patches/); nothing else may differ. `python3 scripts/vendor-patches.py
check` downloads each pristine crate, verifies it against the registry checksum,
applies the patch and fails on any difference, so an undocumented edit cannot
hide in a vendored tree.

Update a crate to a new release with
`python3 scripts/vendor-patches.py refresh <crate> <version>` (it re-applies the
patch and stops if a hunk no longer fits), then `cargo update -p <crate>`. After
changing a vendored file by hand, run `python3 scripts/vendor-patches.py generate
<crate>` and commit the new patch.

| Crate | Version | What the patch changes |
|---|---|---|
| `sqlx-postgres` | 0.9.1 | Keep up to 256 server notices per connection, each cut to 8 KiB, and hand them to the caller through `take_server_notices` with a count of the notices dropped. Reject SCRAM iteration counts above 100,000 and a server nonce that does not extend the client nonce (same cap as postgres-protocol 0.6.12, RUSTSEC-2026-0179). Recognise multirange type codes so unsupported values reach BookiE's explicit refusal path. Resolve type metadata up to 1,024 levels so deep domain and enum chains load. Allow a query to request text results for selected server-formatted scalar types, including when SQLx re-prepares a stale statement. Send protocol CancelRequest packets using a connection's frontend backend key for pooler-safe cancellation. Expose the server's last reported run-time parameters (such as `standard_conforming_strings`) so the editor lexes SQL the way the session does. Two build fixes for the trimmed feature set (a `Json` import path and a dead-code expectation). Turn on TCP keepalive (30 s idle, 10 s interval) on the direct socket. Stop sending `TimeZone=UTC` in the startup message so a session keeps its role or server time zone. Do not read `PGHOSTADDR` from the environment: since 0.9.1 `hostaddr` overrides the dialled address, so an inherited variable would bypass the configured host and SSH tunnel. SQLx 0.9.1 itself keeps quoted `NULL` text in arrays (pull request 4488), rolls back a transaction whose `BEGIN` is cancelled (pull request 4394) and sets `TCP_NODELAY` (pull request 4336). |
| `sqlx-mysql` | 0.9.1 | Expose `COM_RESET_CONNECTION` for pool session isolation and clear invalidated prepared-statement IDs. Count the warnings that OK and EOF packets report and expose the count since the last call through `take_warning_count`. Report `ENUM` and `SET` columns as text even when a collation sets the binary flag, and name `SET` columns. Return a protocol error instead of panicking on a column definition shorter than its fixed 10-byte suffix. Enforce the cleartext authentication opt-in for the initial handshake (SQLx enforces it for authentication switches). Turn on TCP keepalive (30 s idle, 10 s interval) on the direct socket. Refuse the in-band RSA password exchange (`caching_sha2_password` full authentication and `sha256_password`) when the connection is neither TLS nor a local socket, so the password is never encrypted to a public key a network observer could have substituted. A connection through BookiE's SSH tunnel dials a local socket, so it passes this check although only the SSH leg is encrypted: the password is protected as far as the SSH server, and the last hop to the database is the server operator's to secure. Whitespace only elsewhere. SQLx 0.9.1 itself (pull request 4458) returns protocol errors for malformed handshake, ERR, EOF, text and binary row and authentication continue packets, a result set claiming more than 4,096 columns and a packet reassembled from more than 1 GiB of parts. |
| `tiberius` | 0.13.0 | Keep up to 256 informational messages (`PRINT`, `RAISERROR` at severity 10 or below) per connection, each cut to 8 KiB, and hand them to the caller through `Client::take_server_info` with a count of those dropped. After `Client::cancel_query` sends Attention, the drain keeps reading across message boundaries until the `DONE_ATTN` acknowledgement, because SQL Server ends the cancelled request and acknowledges Attention in separate messages. The documentation site sources, examples, tests, workflows, `Cargo.lock` and the changelog are not vendored; the licence files are. |
| `mongodb` | 3.10.0 | Let the TLS layer verify a hostname different from the one it dials, and use native system roots when no CA file is configured. The SCRAM iteration cap and nonce prefix check are in the released crate since 3.10.0. |
| `redis` | 1.8.1 | Let a TLS connection verify a hostname different from the one it dials, so a certificate check survives an SSH tunnel's loopback dial address. Benchmarks, examples, tests, the changelog and `release.toml` are not vendored; the licence file is. |

`sqlx-core` and `sqlx-sqlite` are no longer vendored: SQLx 0.9.1 contains the pool idle-count underflow fix and permits `libsqlite3-sys` 0.40.x.

A released dependency version with these behaviors would let the local copies be dropped; see
[dependency patch guide](../docs/vendor-patches.md).
